open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: What authoritative time source supplies the fresh `marked_at` instant when a mark is created?
options: an injected system clock
an ambient system clock
a timestamp supplied by the caller
a declared authority module
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected system UTC clock.

witness.initial: A placement exists and has no publication mark.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to record a publication.
The deliverer creates M07 and must populate `marked_at`.
outcomes: The service reads its own system clock.
The service uses an instant supplied by the caller or another authority.
witness.observer: A caller or operator reading the stored mark

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark.marked_at
open_points.question: In what representation is `marked_at` stored: offset-aware UTC, UTC without an offset, local time, or another form?
options: offset-aware UTC datetime
UTC datetime without an offset
configured local-time datetime
open_points.default_guess: Store UTC without an offset, consistently with the photo-date convention.

witness.initial: A mark is created at one absolute instant.
events: The deliverer serializes the new mark.
The mark is read after creation.
outcomes: `marked_at` is stored as an offset-aware UTC value such as `2026-11-19T10:00:00+00:00`.
`marked_at` is stored as a UTC value without an offset such as `2026-11-19T10:00:00`.
witness.observer: The mark reader and any generated model validator

open_points.subject: mark operation
open_points.question: How many readings of the time source does one mark operation take, and at what point relative to taking the project lock and writing the record?
options: one reading after the lock is taken
one reading before waiting for the lock
multiple readings with one selected for `marked_at`
open_points.default_guess: Read the clock exactly once after taking the project lock and immediately before building the mark.

witness.initial: Another process holds the project lock while a mark request waits.
events: A mark request begins.
The request waits for the project lock.
The lock is released and the mark is written.
outcomes: `marked_at` records the instant before the wait.
`marked_at` records the instant after the wait when the mark is actually created.
witness.observer: The caller or operator comparing the request time with the stored mark

open_points.subject: A3 rule 2 and A6 rule 2
open_points.text: An absent project lock file and the folders leading to it are the one exception: taking the lock creates them (A6 rules 2 and 4).
open_points.question: Does “the folders leading to it” mean only folders below an already existing configured state folder, or does it include the configured state folder that A6 rule 2 says the service never creates?
options: create only LOCKS_FOLDER and other descendants below the existing state folder
also create the configured state folder
refuse if the configured state folder is absent
open_points.default_guess: Require the configured state folder to exist and create only the lock-related descendants below it.

witness.initial: A placement record already exists, but the configured state folder and therefore the project lock are absent.
events: A caller repeats delivery of the placed content.
The operation reaches the project-lock check.
outcomes: A3 rule 2 is read to require creation of every folder leading to the lock, after which the placement is replayed.
A6 rule 2 is read to prohibit creation of the configured state folder, so the operation is refused with `state_unavailable`.
witness.observer: The caller and the installation operator

open_points.subject: A6 project lock creation
open_points.text: It is not written through a temporary name: it is created in place, exclusively, for reading and writing and without following a link, and once it is found to be a regular file it is given the mode of the imported `LOCK_FILE_MODE` constant, whatever the umask;
open_points.question: When two processes both observe an absent lock and one exclusive creation succeeds while the other receives an already-exists result, must the loser reopen the new file as an existing lock and wait, or treat its creation failure as a refusal?
options: reopen and validate the newly existing file, then wait for its lock
retry the entire lock-opening sequence
refuse the losing call as unable to open the lock file
open_points.default_guess: Reopen and validate the newly existing file, then wait for the operating-system lock.

witness.initial: The project lock file is absent and the folders containing it exist.
events: Process A and process B begin deliveries for the same project.
Both attempt exclusive in-place creation.
Process A creates the file; process B receives an already-exists result.
outcomes: Process B opens the file under the existing-file rule and waits, so both calls proceed serially.
Process B treats the failed exclusive creation as a lock-file failure and returns `state_unavailable`.

open_points.subject: INV-06
open_points.text: INV-06: at most one placement exists per project and source content, and a repeated placement writes nothing.
open_points.question: Must INV-06 be qualified to allow creation of the absent project lock and its permitted folders, as A3 rule 2 now does?
options: qualify “writes nothing” with the lock-scaffolding exception
remove the exception and require replay to create nothing
define lock creation as outside the invariant's meaning of writing
open_points.default_guess: Qualify INV-06 with the same explicit lock-scaffolding exception as A3 rule 2.

witness.initial: A placement exists, but its project lock and lock folder do not.
events: The caller repeats delivery of that source content.
The operation takes the project lock before reading the existing placement.
outcomes: A3 rule 2 creates the folder and lock file and returns `replayed`.
INV-06 permits no write by a repeated placement, so a conforming implementation must not create them.
witness.observer: The filesystem operator and an invariant check

open_points.subject: INV-06 Required tests
open_points.text: INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`).
open_points.question: What must the INV-06 test show about an initially absent project lock, its folders, marks, temporary files, and all other durable state now that replay has a stated lock-scaffolding exception?
options: show that only the permitted lock file and required folders may be added and every other durable entry remains unchanged
pre-create the lock and show that absolutely no durable entry changes
retain the current assertions only for images and placement records
open_points.default_guess: Add a case with an absent lock and assert that only the permitted lock scaffolding is created, while every other durable entry remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

witness.initial: A placement exists while the project lock and lock folder are absent.
events: The required test snapshots only stored images and placement records.
A repeated delivery creates the lock scaffolding and returns `replayed`.
outcomes: The test passes because the image and placement record did not change, without demonstrating the revised invariant's exact exception.
A stronger test checks all durable state and proves that the lock scaffolding is the only change.

open_points.subject: R0-15 repeated delivery guarantee
open_points.text: a repeated delivery creates nothing new
open_points.question: Is the State 0 guarantee revised so that a repeated delivery may create the project lock and its required folders?
options: revise the guarantee with the lock-scaffolding exception
forbid lock creation during replay
treat lock scaffolding as not covered by “nothing new”
open_points.default_guess: Revise the guarantee to state the lock-scaffolding exception explicitly.

witness.initial: A placement exists and the project lock does not.
events: The caller repeats delivery.
The service takes the project lock.
outcomes: The changed A3 rule creates a lock file and folders.
R0-15 says the repeated delivery creates nothing new.
witness.observer: The installation operator inspecting durable state

open_points.subject: P-06 repeated placement guarantee
open_points.text: One placement exists per project and source content; repeating it changes nothing.
open_points.question: Does “changes nothing” exclude the newly permitted creation of a project lock and its folders, or must P-06 be amended?
options: amend P-06 with the lock-scaffolding exception
remove the A3 exception
declare locking infrastructure outside the meaning of the accepted result
open_points.default_guess: Amend P-06 with the same explicit exception.

witness.initial: A placement exists with no project lock file.
events: The placement is repeated.
Taking the lock creates the lock file and missing lock folders.
outcomes: The changed A3 rule changes durable filesystem state.
P-06 says repeating the placement changes nothing.
witness.observer: The owner or a conformance test inspecting the state folder

open_points.subject: M04 PhotoPlacement
open_points.text: A repeated placement returns it and writes nothing (P-06).
open_points.question: Must M04's meaning permit the project-lock and folder creation introduced by A3 rule 2?
options: change the model text to allow only the lock-scaffolding exception
require the lock to pre-exist before any replay
keep “writes nothing” and remove the A3 exception
open_points.default_guess: Change the model text to allow only the project-lock scaffolding exception.

witness.initial: M04 already exists, but its project has no lock file.
events: A repeated placement is requested.
The service creates and takes the lock before returning M04.
outcomes: A3 rule 2 permits the lock and folders to be written.
M04 says returning the repeated placement writes nothing.
witness.observer: A generated implementation or test using the model contract
